sections.h2: Why is Ennis a different kind of market from the border cities?
sections.html:
Ennis has grown quickly and carries higher home values, so sellers here compete with new construction. The federal estimate puts the city at 25,694 residents in July 2025, a 27.6% jump from an April 2020 base of 20,133.

A fast-growing town gives an older house two kinds of buyers: families who prefer an established lot and investors who see rental demand. A direct sale suits someone who cannot wait for either. Think about how your house stacks up against new homes nearby before you pick an asking price.

  • Direct buyer: house taken as is, date agreed together.
  • Agent listing: the broadest audience, with showings.
  • Family sale: quick on price, still needs a recorded deed.

sections.h2: What does federal data show about Ennis housing?
sections.html:
Ennis reports a higher home value than El Paso or Eagle Pass, a longer commute and a larger share of residents in the workforce. The table lists the details.

A 27.6 minute average trip suggests many residents work outside town, so a listing that explains road access to larger job centers can help. Keep the description to facts you can check.

sections.h2: Who is buying in Ennis, and what do they earn?
sections.html:
Buyers lean toward households with children and steady jobs. Federal data lists 25.7% of residents under 18, 12.7% aged 65 or older, 69.0% of adults in the labor force, median household income of $75,074 and per capita income of $33,059.

Owner costs run $1,991 a month with a mortgage and $670 without, so a buyer financing a home needs an income near the local median to carry a typical payment. Poverty is 10.9%, and 19.0% of residents under 65 have no health insurance. Among adults 25 and older, 78.2% finished high school and 20.7% hold a bachelor's degree.

Stability helps sellers too. About 89.2% of residents lived at the same address a year before, so streets feel settled. A third, 33.8%, use another language at home, so a bilingual listing is useful.

  • Families: yards, schools and a quiet street.
  • Commuters: road access toward larger job centers.
  • Investors: a rent near $1,362 weighed against price.

sections.h2: What permits does the City of Ennis require?
sections.html:
The city requires a permit before anyone builds, alters, enlarges, moves, demolishes or repairs a structure inside city limits. Buyers ask for those records, so gather them early.

  • Accessory buildings over 120 square feet.
  • Demolition and moving a structure.
  • Drive approaches and irrigation systems.
  • Fences taller than 8 feet.
  • Signs, swimming pools and spas.

Planning and Development is at 108 W. Knox Street, (972) 875-6442, open weekdays from eight to five. Its page links a Historic District information page, a zoning verification letter and a tool to find your zoning district. Use them to answer a buyer who wants to add a shed or a pool.

sections.h2: How large is Ennis, and what will shoppers notice?
sections.html:
Ennis covers 32.50 land square miles, up from 27.65 in 2010, with 620.2 residents per square mile in 2020. That is far more room per resident than in the border cities, so lot size and yard space are real selling points.

Retail sales reached about $631 million in 2022, or $27,591 per person, and food and lodging sales were near $79 million. With 7,982 households and 88.6% on broadband, most buyers begin online, so show clear photos, an accurate floor plan and the age of the roof and cooling system.

  • Lot size: mention it, since density is low.
  • Photos: shoot in daylight and include the back yard.
  • Records: list recent roof, plumbing or cooling work.

sections.h2: How long does a buyer wait on an Ennis permit?
sections.html:
The city prints plan review times by project size, which helps a buyer who plans renovations after closing.

  • Small residential projects and minor additions: 1 to 3 days.
  • New residential construction and major additions: 3 to 10 days.
  • Small commercial projects and minor additions: 3 to 10 days.
  • New commercial construction and major additions: 14 to 28 days.

Planning and Development says workload can change these times. The permit holder schedules inspections, and the city lists an online portal for permits and inspections. If your buyer wants to add a room, quote these ranges so the buyer can plan the timeline.

sections.h2: How do tax bills figure into an Ennis sale?
sections.html:
The appraisal district sets value, local units set rates, and a lien for the year attaches January 1. A sale later in the year divides the bill at the closing table.

The Comptroller describes a school homestead exemption, added relief for owners 65 or older or disabled, and a 10% yearly cap on a homestead's appraised value. Bills reach owners in autumn and may be paid in two halves.

  • Ask the county tax office for your balance.
  • Request a tax certificate for closing.
  • Protest a value in spring if it looks wrong.

sections.h2: What can an Ennis seller do to prepare the house?
sections.html:
Pull together the records a title company asks for, and present the house the way a buyer comparing it with new construction would want to see it.

  • Deed, loan payoff letter and latest tax bill.
  • Permit and inspection records for pools, fences, sheds and drive approaches.
  • The zoning district for your lot from the city's lookup tool.
  • Receipts for roof, cooling and plumbing work.

A median gross rent of $1,362 makes Ennis appealing to landlords, so mention whether the house suits a tenant. If your street sits in a historic area, ask the planning office about exterior rules before you promise anything to a buyer. Clean, bright rooms and a tidy yard matter in a town where buyers can compare your house against new builds on the edge of town.

Take time to walk the lot with the city's zoning lookup open, and note any setbacks or easements the buyer should know about. If you plan to leave appliances, list them in the contract so nothing is disputed at the final walk-through. Ask your title company to run a quick check for open permits or liens a few days before listing, which gives you time to fix surprises without pressure from a contract deadline. Photographs taken in daylight, with the yard and the street visible, help buyers who are comparing your house with newer ones.

sections.h2: What about foreclosure, deeds and inheritance in Ennis?
sections.html:
A sale before an auction is allowed, and the lender is paid from the proceeds. After a default notice you have a short window to catch up, and a sale notice must precede the monthly auction by weeks.

The county clerk files the deed after notary acknowledgment and charges by the page. For an inherited house, the State Law Library describes several routes for smaller estates, and your title company will say which proof it needs.

faqs.q: How fast can an Ennis sale close?
faqs.a: The buyer and the title company set the date. Ask for it in writing and keep your payoff letter ready.

faqs.q: Does Ennis require a permit for an old addition?
faqs.a: Ask Planning and Development at (972) 875-6442. The city requires a permit for work that alters or enlarges a structure.

faqs.q: Does Ennis have a historic district?
faqs.a: The city website lists a Historic District information page and a Historic Landmark Commission. Ask whether your address is covered.

faqs.q: Who sets property tax for an Ennis home?
faqs.a: Local units set rates and the appraisal district sets value. Ask the county tax office for your balance.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ennis house with a mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes. The loan is paid from the proceeds at closing, so request a payoff statement from your lender.
